newsitem.title: USA: Pinole, Calif., settles dispute with tax group.
newsitem.headline: Pinole, Calif., settles dispute with tax group.

text.p: The northern California city of Pinole has settled a legal dispute with a prominent taxpayers group by agreeing to place its property-transfer tax on the November ballot, city attorneys said on Tuesday.

The Pinole settlement was the first by a city sued by the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association over alleged violations of California's Proposition 62, said attorney Steve Mayer, who represents Pinole and other cities targeted by the association.
Last year, the association filed a lawsuit against Pinole, challenging its utility-user and property-transfer taxes.
The lawsuit asserted that the taxes were not approved by voters as required under Proposition 62.
The proposition requires two-thirds voter approval for special tax increases and majority approval for the imposition of general tax increases.
Pinole was one of several California cities sued by the association for alleged violations of Proposition 62.
A judge hearing the case tossed out the association's challenge to Pinole's utility-user tax, but the judge let the association's challenge to the property-transfer tax stand.
To avoid a prolonged fight in court over the property-transfer tax, the city agreed to place the levy on the November ballot, Mayer said.
Pinole's property-transfer tax generates between $200,000 to $300,000 a year. The utility-user tax, by contrast, raises an estimated $1.0 million a year.
Jonathan Coupal, director of legal affairs for the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association, said he may still file an appeal to have the Pinole utility-user tax placed on the ballot.
The association has lobbied to pass several controversial tax-limitation measures in California, including Proposition 62 and last November's Proposition 218.
